paper_metadata.title: Evaluation of hematological markers in minor head trauma in the emergency room

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a retrospective case-control design rather than a prospective cohort. While inclusion/exclusion criteria are clear, the use of a fixed number (100 cases vs 100 controls) suggests a convenience sample rather than consecutive recruitment, which may not fully represent the natural prevalence or spectrum of the target population.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: patients who presented to the emergency room with minor head trauma... GCS of 15, loss of consciousness for less than 20 min, and no neurological deficits
items.reasoning: The authors clearly define the clinical characteristics of the target population (minor head trauma patients in an ER setting).

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: This retrospective study included 100 patients with pathologies present on their CT scans and a control group consisting of 100 patients with a normal CT.
items.reasoning: The study identifies patients retrospectively from files. However, it does not specify if these were consecutive patients or how the 100/100 split was selected from the total pool of admissions, introducing potential selection bias.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: This retrospective study was conducted between 1 January 2013 and 31 December 2014
items.reasoning: The specific two-year window is clearly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: our university research hospital emergency department... Mugla Sitki Kocman Universty Medicine School, Mugla, Turkey
items.reasoning: The specific hospital and geographic location are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients whose GCS scores were below 15, patients who had multiple traumas, chest pain, anemia, or chronic renal failure were excluded from the study.
items.reasoning: The study provides specific clinical criteria for both inclusion (GCS 15, isolated trauma) and exclusion (comorbidities that affect hematological markers).

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: As a retrospective file review, the total number of eligible patients during the period is not mentioned, so the participation/inclusion rate cannot be calculated.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The mean age of the patients was 35.25 ± 20.25, and among these patients, 151 (75.5 %) were men and 49 (24.5 %) were women.
items.reasoning: Table 1 and the Results section provide age, sex, and baseline lab values for the groups.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Because the study is a retrospective analysis of ER records where the 'outcome' (CT pathology) is determined at the same visit as the 'predictor' (blood draw), there is virtually no loss to follow-up in the traditional longitudinal sense.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 200 patients who presented with isolated minor head trauma were included in our study.
items.reasoning: The study analyzed all 200 patients selected for the case and control groups.

items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Not applicable for this study design as it is a cross-sectional retrospective analysis of a single ER visit.

items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (hematological markers) are objective laboratory values measured using standardized automated equipment, minimizing measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: analyzed under room temperature in the biochemistry laboratory using Pentra DF Nexus, Hariba Medical device, and troponin T was measured with Roche Hitachi Cobas E 601 device.
items.reasoning: The specific markers and the equipment used to measure them are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Blood test results of the patients at their first admission to the emergency service of our hospital were reviewed.
items.reasoning: Standardized laboratory assays are highly reliable and do not rely on subjective recall.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: the troponin T cut-off value of 6.16 lead to 90 % specificity, and setting the NLR cut-off value at 4.29 resulted in a specificity of 90 %.
items.reasoning: The authors used ROC curves to determine cut-offs. These are data-dependent cut-points, which can lead to over-optimistic results if not validated in an independent sample.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Blood test results of the patients at their first admission to the emergency service of our hospital were reviewed.
items.reasoning: All tests were performed in the same hospital laboratory using the same devices.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: The results of the routine complete blood count and biochemical tests taken from these patients... were recorded.
items.reasoning: The study implies complete data for the 200 included patients.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no mention of missing data or imputation methods.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (CT pathology) is an objective imaging standard, and the study utilized multiple specialists (radiologist, neurosurgeon) to confirm findings, reducing the risk of misclassification.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: epidural hematoma, subdural hematoma, intracranial contusion and hematomas, subarachnoid hemorrhage, cerebral edema, pneumocephalus, and skull fractures were considered pathologies.
items.reasoning: The study explicitly lists what constitutes a positive CT outcome.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients CT were examined by a neurosurgeon and a radiologist and an otolaryngologist to select the isolated head trauma.
items.reasoning: The use of 16-slice CT and review by multiple specialists ensures high validity.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Unenhanced CT scanning was performed with 16-slice Toshiba Asteion TSX-021B... within 30-60 min of emergency department admission.
items.reasoning: All patients underwent the same imaging protocol within a similar timeframe.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study excluded major confounders like chronic renal failure and anemia, it did not perform multivariable adjustment for other potential confounders like age or mechanism of injury in the primary analysis of the markers.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: Age, Sex... Patients whose GCS scores were below 15, patients who had multiple traumas, chest pain, anemia, or chronic renal failure were excluded
items.reasoning: Basic demographics and major medical comorbidities were measured or used as exclusion criteria, but other factors like medication use (anticoagulants) were not mentioned.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: The mean age of the patients was 35.25 ± 20.25, and among these patients, 151 (75.5 %) were men
items.reasoning: Age and sex are standard variables.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: We retrospectively examined the files of patients
items.reasoning: Demographics and medical history in hospital files are generally reliable.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: When reviewing the files of patients, detailed neurological examination, the causes of trauma, and patients' complaints... were recorded
items.reasoning: Data collection was uniform across the retrospective cohort.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No mention of missing confounder data.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: a control group consisting of 100 patients with a normal CT.
items.reasoning: The study used a control group and exclusion criteria to limit confounding, but did not match cases and controls on age or sex.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: Parametric tests (independent samples test) were used... non-parametric tests (Mann–Whitney U test) were used
items.reasoning: The primary results are based on univariable comparisons. Although 'backward logistic regression' is mentioned in the methods, the results primarily report p-values for individual markers without showing adjusted odds ratios.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study reports significant findings but lacks a clear pre-specified protocol. The use of data-driven cut-points for ROC analysis without internal or external validation increases the risk of overestimating the prognostic accuracy of the markers.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Quantitative variables were given as mean ± SD... Parametric tests (independent samples test) were used with normally distributed data
items.reasoning: The statistical methods are standard and described.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: The relationship between the demographic and hematological parameters between the two groups was examined by backward logistic regression analysis.
items.reasoning: While regression is mentioned, the criteria for variable entry and the final model results are not fully detailed in the results section.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: The normalcy of distribution was evaluated when comparing the groups.
items.reasoning: The use of Mann-Whitney U and Independent T-tests is appropriate for comparing two groups.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Table 1... Table 2... Table 4
items.reasoning: The authors report results for all markers mentioned in the methods, but the lack of a prospective trial registration makes it difficult to ensure no other markers were tested and omitted.
